content.comment_body: I'm facing an issue I can't resolve alone. I have a button that switches on a motor. When the motor starts, the button turns red to indicate the operator can turn it off at any time. However, if the operator forgets to shut it down, I want to add a countdown timer so the motor will stop automatically when time runs out. The challenge is, after the timer turns off the motor, the button remains red instead of switching back to green. I haven't found a way to set the variable's output low at the end of the delay, as it interferes with the button's input logic. I appreciate any advice. PS: This is similar to an earlier issue I had with analog values and updating parameters with [product_name] and [product_name] in [company_name]'s forum, which was solved by VM mapping, but I don't think that's possible here. Thanks again.
For me, the issue is that I don't see what you've done in the [product_name] project. Could you upload your [product_name] project file?
I've attached an example. Thank you for your support.

What you're aiming for isn't possible in this scenario. You can't write back to the same address of the network input. You'll need a different solution. Instead of the switch button, consider using a push button connected to a pulse relay's trigger input. Replace the switch-off delay and positive edge logic with a switch-on delay. Connect the output of this delay to the R input of the pulse relay. Alongside the push button, add a switch button that changes color with Q1.
Thank you for your guidance and time. The solution works very well and the code is easy to follow. Thanks again.
Glad to hear it works as you wanted. That sounds promising.
